atomizer_prompt.system: Split compound triplets into atomic facts. Preserve subject/predicate/object roles exactly.
atomizer_prompt.instructions:
You are given ONE knowledge-graph triplet (subject | predicate | object) taken from a response, and the response as context when it is available. Decide whether the triplet states one fact or several, and split it only where it states several. Most triplets are already one fact; splitting is rare. In doubt, keep.

Always:
- Conserve the meaning exactly. Together the parts say exactly what the triplet says: nothing dropped, nothing added.
- Use the triplet's own words, in its order and direction. Never paraphrase, never swap subject and object, never take a fact from the context. You may repeat shared words in each part and add only joining words (is, are, has, of, for, in, on, at, that).
- Copy into every part whatever governs all of it: a hedge ("may", "likely", "I think"), a negation, a condition ("if", "when", "unless"), a place, date or heading, and "only".
- Every part must read alone as a sensible claim the triplet states. If one part does not, keep the triplet.

Split, one triplet per part, in these cases:
1. A list whose items each hold on their own: (the cream | soothes | burns and rashes) -> (the cream | soothes | burns) + (the cream | soothes | rashes). "Etc.", "and more" and "among others" are not items.
2. A class with examples: one triplet per example, each keeping the class: (the bakery | sells | breads such as rye and spelt) -> (the bakery | sells | breads such as rye) + (the bakery | sells | breads such as spelt). Never a separate triplet saying that the example belongs to the class, unless that is what the triplet itself says.
3. Paired lists ("respectively"): pair the items in order, one triplet per pair, never every combination.
4. An "or" under a negation, a permission or the condition of an "if" applies to each item: (guests | may bring | a dog or a cat) -> (guests | may bring | a dog) + (guests | may bring | a cat); (visitors | must not bring | glass or metal) -> (visitors | must not bring | glass) + (visitors | must not bring | metal).
5. "Not X but Y": the negative and the positive are two triplets, each with the shared subject and verb: (the tower | was built | not in 1890 but in 1902) -> (the tower | was not built in | 1890) + (the tower | was built in | 1902).
6. Two clauses joined by "although", "but" or "while": one triplet per clause; the contrast word gives none.
7. A detail that adds a fact about a thing already named (an apposition, a parenthesis, a "which" clause set off by commas, a title before a name) becomes its own triplet about that thing, and the host triplet loses it, but only if the host is then still about the same thing and still true: (Lake Corran, the deepest lake in the county | freezes in | winter) -> (Lake Corran | is | the deepest lake in the county) + (Lake Corran | freezes in | winter).
8. A judgement inside a noun phrase: (the beautiful bridge | links | the two towns) -> (the bridge | is | beautiful) + (the bridge | links | the two towns).
9. A factive verb ("knows that", "realised that", "regrets that", "is aware that") states its complement as true: keep the whole triplet and add the complement as its own triplet: (the guides | know that | the pass closes in October) -> (the guides | know that | the pass closes in October) + (the pass | closes in | October). Not for "believes", "thinks", "claims" or "says", and not for a source that shows or finds something ("tests show that X" stays one triplet).
10. A purpose the advice does not need is its own triplet: (you | should water the lawn early in the morning | to reduce evaporation) -> (you | should water | the lawn early in the morning) + (watering the lawn early in the morning | reduces | evaporation). If the advice is not true as meant without the purpose, the purpose is a condition and stays: (you | should keep | the receipt to get a refund).
11. A chain of causes the triplet states gives one triplet per stated link. Events joined by a bare "so" or "therefore" are each a triplet, with no causal triplet between them: (heavy rain | flooded the road, so | the bus was late) -> (heavy rain | flooded | the road) + (the bus | was | late).
12. Steps of an instruction: one triplet per step; a step that depends on the one before keeps its "first … then" inside.

Keep as one triplet in these cases:
1. Items that only hold together: a shared value or sum ("one €20 charge for delivery and assembly"), a mixture or blend, a comparison or relation between the items ("the same for members and guests", "Mia and Tom married each other"), a pair ("both").
2. Items that name all the members of a set: (the founders of the band | were | Ada and Ben), or a bare list answering "which …". The triplet says these are all.
3. Any other "A or B": (the parcel | must be sent by | post or courier) stays. So does an "or" that gives a second name or one meaning.
4. A rule with its exception: (all members except trainees | may vote at | the meeting) stays.
5. A condition (if, when, once, unless, depending on, a deadline with "by"), and an "even if".
6. A detail that says which thing is meant: (cars with petrol engines | are banned from | the old town) stays. So does a modifier that could belong to either of two nouns, and "former", "fake" or "toy".
7. A means or manner ("by closing the windows"), a comparison with its baseline, a rank with its class.
8. A number with its approximation word, bound or margin; a range; one value in two units; a statistic with its population and comparison; a change with both values, its direction and date ("rose from $2 to $3 in 2019").
9. A second name for the same thing, in brackets or apposition: (the European Space Agency (ESA) | launched | the probe) stays; no triplet for the name.
10. A view or report with its holder: (critics | argue that | the new museum is too small and too dark) stays one triplet, and so does "experts agree that …".
11. A fixed name or compound ("Terms and Conditions", "New Zealand"), and stacked adjectives that describe one thing ("a small, thin, flat stone").
12. Two lists that would have to be multiplied into every combination: (the north and south gauges | recorded | rain and hail) stays, unless the triplet says which goes with which.

Think first, then decide. Return JSON with exactly these three fields:
- reasoning: one short sentence naming the case (one fact, a list, a class with examples, items that hold together, ...).
- is_atomic: true to keep the triplet, false to split it.
- split: when is_atomic is false, the parts, each with subject, predicate and object; otherwise an empty array.
